blocks.text: Yeh chapter 7 (Waves and Vibrations) ke poore chapter se practice long questions (tafseeli sawal) hain, Board ke long question ki shakal mein: har 5 number ke theory sawal (definition, wazahat, derivation) ke baad usi mauzu ka 3 number ka numerical hai. Har sawal ka model jawab hai; numericals qadam ba qadam hal kiye gaye hain.

blocks.prompt:
1 What is a wave? Define amplitude, frequency, wavelength, period and phase of a wave, and derive the relation between the speed, frequency and wavelength of a wave. (5 marks)
(Wave kya hai? Wave ke amplitude, frequency, wavelength, period aur phase ki definitions likhein, aur wave ki speed, frequency aur wavelength ka ta'alluq derive karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Wave: aik baqaida khalal (disturbance) jo energy le kar source se phailta hai. Medium mein zarraat apni jagah oopar neeche ya aage peeche hilte hain aur pattern phailta hai (maslan talaab par ripples).

Zarre ka displacement: rest / equilibrium position se kisi khaas simt mein faasla. y-axis par displacement aur x-axis par energy ke safar ki simt mein faasla lagane se waveform banti hai (Fig. 7.2).

Parameters:
1. Amplitude (A): equilibrium position se zyada se zyada displacement.
2. Frequency (f): aik second mein oscillations (cycles) ki tadaad.
3. Wavelength (λ): do lagataar milte julte, aik phase wale points ka faasla.
4. Period (T): aik oscillation poora karne ka waqt; T = 1/f.
5. Phase (θ): kisi waqt par wave par point ki nisbati position.

Wave ki speed: crest aik period T mein aik wavelength λ chalti hai, is liye
v = λ/T
Chunke 1/T = f,
v = fλ ... (7.1)

book_ref.quote: The waves can be described by the following parameters:

blocks.prompt:
2 A radio transmitter operating at 1.2 MHz sends waves of wavelength 250 m. Find (i) the speed of the radio waves (ii) the wavelength of a second transmitter operating at 600 kHz (iii) the period of the first wave. (3 marks)
(1.2 MHz par chalne wala radio transmitter 250 m wavelength ki waves bhejta hai. Nikalein: (i) radio waves ki speed (ii) 600 kHz par chalne wale doosre transmitter ki wavelength (iii) pehli wave ka period.)
blocks.explanation: Dono signals ki speed aik hai; v = fλ, phir λ = v/f aur T = 1/f.

book_ref.quote: What is the wavelength for a transmitter operating at 1000 kHz

blocks.prompt:
3 State the principle of superposition of waves. Explain the resultant displacement when two overlapping waves are (i) in the same phase (ii) in opposite phase, and extend the principle to n waves. Which phenomena does it lead to? (5 marks)
(Waves ke superposition ka usool bayan karein. Do milne wali waves ka resultant displacement wazeh karein jab woh (i) aik phase mein hon (ii) ulat phase mein hon, aur usool ko n waves tak barhayein. Is se kaun se mazahir paida hote hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Usool: Agar medium ke zarre par aik saath do waves amal karein to zarre ka resultant displacement un ke alag displacements ka algebraic majmua hota hai. Displacements jama ho kar naya wave pattern banate hain (Fig. 7.4).

(i) Aik phase (Fig. 7.4 a):
y = y₁ + y₂
Agar y₁ = y₂ to y = 2y₁ (ya 2y₂): bara resultant.

(ii) Ulat phase (Fig. 7.4 b):
y = y₁ + (−y₂) = y₁ − y₂
Agar y₁ = y₂ to y = 0: waves khatam.

n waves: agar n waves ke displacements y₁, y₂, …, yₙ hon to
y = y₁ + y₂ + … + yₙ
ya y(x,t) = y₁(x,t) + y₂(x,t) + … + yₙ(x,t), jahan y(x,t) point x aur waqt t par resultant displacement hai.
Yeh usool linear waves, yani chhote amplitude wali waves par laagu hai.

Mazahir:
1. Aik frequency, aik simt: interference.
2. Thori mukhtalif frequencies, aik simt: beats.
3. Barabar frequency, ulat simtein: stationary waves.

book_ref.quote: In other words, the displacements of the individual waves are added together to form a new wave pattern

blocks.prompt:
4 Find the resultant displacement of a particle when (i) two waves of displacement 4 mm each meet in the same phase (ii) the same two waves meet in opposite phase (iii) three waves give displacements of +6 mm, −2 mm and +3 mm at the same instant. (3 marks)
(Zarre ka resultant displacement nikalein jab (i) 4 mm displacement wali do waves aik phase mein milein (ii) wahi do waves ulat phase mein milein (iii) teen waves aik lamhe +6 mm, −2 mm aur +3 mm displacement dein.)
blocks.explanation: Displacements ko alaamat ke saath jama karein: aik phase mein jama, ulat phase mein tafreeq.

book_ref.quote: where y₁ = amplitude of wave 1, y₂ = amplitude of wave 2 and y = resultant amplitude.

blocks.prompt:
5 Define interference. Describe an experiment with two loudspeakers and a CRO to observe interference of sound waves, and obtain the conditions for constructive and destructive interference in terms of path difference. (5 marks)
(Interference ki definition likhein. Do loudspeakers aur CRO ke saath sound waves ka interference dekhne ka tajurba bayan karein, aur path difference ki shakal mein constructive aur destructive interference ki sharait hasil karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Interference: aik frequency wali, aik simt mein chalti do waves ka superposition.

Apparatus (Fig. 7.5 a): Do loudspeakers S₁ aur S₂ aik hi Audio Generator (AG) se chalte hain, is liye fixed frequency ki harmonic sound dete aur aik phase mein vibrate karte hain (coherent sources). Sensitive Cathode Ray Oscilloscope (CRO) se jura microphone sound pakarta hai; CRO signal ko waveform ki shakal mein dikhata hai. Microphone speakers ke saamne mukhtalif points par rakha jata hai (Fig. 7.5 b).

Constructive interference: P₁, P₃, P₅ par compression compression se aur rarefaction rarefaction se milta hai. Displacements jama hote hain aur CRO par bara displacement (Fig. 7.5 c). P₁ par:
ΔS = S₂P₁ − S₁P₁ = 4½λ − 3½λ = λ
P₃ aur P₅ par ΔS = 0 aur −λ. Yani jab path difference wavelength ka poora multiple ho:
ΔS = nλ, n = 0, ±1, ±2, ±3, …

Destructive interference: P₂ aur P₄ par compression rarefaction se milta hai; dono khatam aur CRO par sifr displacement (Fig. 7.5 d). P₂ par:
ΔS = S₂P₂ − S₁P₂ = 4λ − 3½λ = ½λ
Yani path difference λ/2 ka taaq (odd) multiple:
ΔS = (2n + 1)λ/2, n = 0, ±1, ±2, ±3, …

book_ref.quote: An experimental set up to observe interference effect of sound waves is shown in Fig. 7.5(a).

blocks.prompt:
6 Two loudspeakers 1.2 m apart are driven by the same generator at 850 Hz. A microphone moved along a line parallel to and 1.6 m from the line joining the speakers gives maximum loudness at the centre and again when it is directly opposite one speaker. Find the wavelength and the speed of sound. (3 marks)
(1.2 m door do loudspeakers aik hi generator se 850 Hz par chalte hain. Speakers wali line ke mutawazi 1.6 m door line par chalta microphone markaz par aur phir aik speaker ke bilkul saamne zyada aawaz deta hai. Wavelength aur sound ki speed nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: S₁ ke saamne markaz ke baad agla oonchi aawaz ka point hai, is liye wahan path difference λ hai; S₂P Pythagoras se.

book_ref.quote: Now, we calculate values of S₂P₁ from right angle triangle S₁S₂P₁

steps: S₁S₂ = 1.2 m, S₁P = 1.6 m, f = 850 Hz

blocks.prompt:
7 Explain how stationary waves are formed by two waves moving along a string in opposite directions. Show that nodes are λ/2 apart and that a node and the next antinode are λ/4 apart. How is energy held in a stationary wave? (5 marks)
(Wazeh karein ke string par ulat simton mein chalti do waves se stationary waves kaise banti hain. Dikhayein ke nodes λ/2 door aur node aur agla antinode λ/4 door hote hain. Stationary wave mein energy kaise rehti hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Stationary (standing) waves aik jagah oscillate karti hain, aage nahi barhteen. Yeh aik frequency aur amplitude wali do ulat simt mein chalti waves ke superposition se banti hain; nodes aur antinodes apni jagah qaim rehte hain.

Banna (Fig. 7.6): Fig. 7.6 (a) aur (b) string par aisi do waves t = 0, T/4, T/2, 3T/4 aur T par dikhati hain. Points 1, 2, …, 7 aapas mein λ/4 door hain. Un ka resultant displacement superposition se nikalta hai.

Nodes: Fig. 7.6 (c) mein points 1, 3, 5, 7 ka resultant displacement har lamhe sifr hai. Yeh nodes hain. 1 aur 3 ke darmiyan do qadam λ/4 ke hain, is liye lagataar nodes ka faasla λ/2 hai.

Antinodes: Fig. 7.6 (d) mein points 2, 4, 6 dono waves ke amplitudes ke majmue jitne amplitude se hilte hain. Yeh antinodes hain, nodes ke beech mein aur aapas mein λ/2 door. Node se agla antinode λ/4 door hai.

Energy: wave mein energy zarraat ki harkat se chalti hai. Nodes hamesha saakin hain, is liye energy un se aage nahi jaati aur nodes ke darmiyan 'khari' rehti hai. Antinodes par intehai displacement par energy poori potential aur equilibrium se guzarte waqt poori kinetic hoti hai.

book_ref.quote: Let us consider the superposition of two waves moving along a string in opposite directions.

blocks.prompt:
8 Two waves, each of amplitude 3 mm, frequency 80 Hz and speed 48 m s⁻¹, travel along a string in opposite directions and form a stationary wave. Find (i) the wavelength (ii) the distance between consecutive nodes (iii) the distance between a node and the next antinode (iv) the amplitude at an antinode. (3 marks)
(3 mm amplitude, 80 Hz frequency aur 48 m s⁻¹ speed wali do waves string par ulat simton mein chal kar stationary wave banati hain. Nikalein: (i) wavelength (ii) lagataar nodes ka faasla (iii) node aur agle antinode ka faasla (iv) antinode par amplitude.)
blocks.explanation: v = fλ se λ, phir λ/2 aur λ/4; antinode ka amplitude dono amplitudes ka majmua.

book_ref.quote: They are situated midway between the nodes and are λ/2 apart.

steps: Node se agla antinode = λ/4 = 0.15 m

blocks.prompt:
9 A string of length l is stretched by clamping its ends with tension F. Explain the stationary waves set up when it is plucked (i) at its middle point (ii) at one quarter of its length, and derive the frequency in each case. (5 marks)
(Lambai l ki string ke sire kas kar tension F di gayi hai. Stationary waves wazeh karein jab string ko (i) beech se (ii) lambai ke chauthai hisse se chheda jaye, aur har soorat mein frequency derive karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Lambai l ki string jis ke sire kase hon aur tension F ho.

(i) Beech se chherna (Fig. 7.7 a): beech se do transverse waves nikalti hain, aik har sire ki taraf. Kase hue siron se reflect ho kar stationary waves banti hain. Kase siron par harkat nahi hoti, is liye wahan nodes aur beech mein aik antinode: string aik loop mein. Lagataar nodes ka faasla λ/2 hai, is liye
l = λ₁/2
λ₁ = 2l ... (7.2)
String par waves ki speed tension F aur fi unit lambai mass m par munhasir hai (chherne ki jagah par nahi):
v = √(F/m) ... (7.3)
f₁ = v/λ₁ = v/2l
f₁ = (1/2l)√(F/m) ... (7.4)

(ii) Chauthai lambai se chherna (Fig. 7.7 b): string antinode ki jagah se chheri jaati hai, is liye do loops mein vibrate karti hai. Har loop λ₂/2 lamba:
l = λ₂/2 + λ₂/2 = 2(λ₂/2)
λ₂ = l
Wavelength pehli soorat ki aadhi hai. Speed v wahi hai (sirf F aur m par munhasir), is liye
f₂ = v/λ₂ = v/l
2 se zarb aur taqseem: f₂ = 2v/2l
Chunke f₁ = v/2l, f₂ = 2f₁
Yani do loops mein frequency aik loop se dugni hai.

book_ref.quote: If the string is plucked at its middle point, two transverse waves will originate from this point.

blocks.prompt:
10 A string 0.80 m long has a mass per unit length of 0.010 kg m⁻¹ and is stretched with a tension of 64 N. Find (i) the speed of transverse waves on it (ii) its fundamental frequency (iii) its frequency when plucked at one quarter of its length. (3 marks)
(0.80 m lambi string ka fi unit lambai mass 0.010 kg m⁻¹ hai aur use 64 N tension se kasa gaya hai. Nikalein: (i) us par transverse waves ki speed (ii) fundamental frequency (iii) chauthai lambai se chherne par frequency.)
blocks.explanation: v = √(F/m), phir f₁ = v/2l; chauthai se chherne par do loops, f₂ = 2f₁.

book_ref.quote: Knowing the speed v and wavelength λ₁, the frequency f₁ of the waves is

steps: Chauthai se chherna: do loops, f₂ = 2f₁ = 100 Hz
blocks.final_answer: v = 80 m s⁻¹; f₁ = 50 Hz; f₂ = 100 Hz

blocks.prompt:
11 Show that a stretched string vibrating in n loops has frequency fₙ = nf₁ and wavelength λₙ = 2l/n. Explain the harmonic series, quantization of frequencies, and how the frequency of a string on a musical instrument is changed. (5 marks)
(Sabit karein ke n loops mein vibrate karti kasi string ki frequency fₙ = nf₁ aur wavelength λₙ = 2l/n hoti hai. Harmonic series, frequencies ki quantization aur musical saaz ki string ki frequency badalne ka tareeqa wazeh karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Farz karein string n loops mein resonate kare, (n + 1) nodes aur n antinodes ke saath. Har loop do lagataar nodes ka faasla λₙ/2 hai, is liye
l = n(λₙ/2)
λₙ = 2l/n ... (7.6)
Speed v = √(F/m) har mode mein aik hai, is liye
fₙ = v/λₙ = n(v/2l)
fₙ = nf₁ ... (7.5), ya fₙ ∝ n, jahan n = 1, 2, 3, …
Zyada loops mein f barhti aur λ chhoti hoti hai, magar fλ hamesha v ke barabar.

Harmonic series: stationary waves ki alag alag frequencies f₁, 2f₁, 3f₁, …, nf₁. Sab se kam f₁ fundamental (pehla harmonic); f₂ = 2f₁ doosra harmonic, waghaira.

Frequencies ki quantization: resonance frequencies ke darmiyan chhalang (quantum jump) hai; fₙ = nf₁, n poora number. Stationary waves sirf inhi frequencies par banti hain jo tension, lambai aur fi unit lambai mass se tay hoti hain; baaqi waves jaldi damp ho jaati hain.

Musical saaz: frequency tension badal kar (guitar ya violin ke pegs kas kar) ya lambai badal kar (neck par ungliyan chala kar thirakne wala hissa chhota bara kar) badli jaati hai.

book_ref.quote: Thus, we can say that if the string is made to vibrate in n loops

blocks.prompt:
12 A string 1.5 m long, fixed at both ends, vibrates in three segments at a frequency of 150 Hz. Find (i) the wavelength (ii) the fundamental frequency (iii) the speed of the waves (iv) the number of nodes and antinodes. (3 marks)
(Dono siron se bandhi 1.5 m lambi string 150 Hz par teen hisson mein vibrate karti hai. Nikalein: (i) wavelength (ii) fundamental frequency (iii) waves ki speed (iv) nodes aur antinodes ki tadaad.)
blocks.explanation: Teen segments yani n = 3: λₙ = 2l/n, fₙ = nf₁ aur v = fλ; n loops mein (n + 1) nodes aur n antinodes.

book_ref.quote: (ii) If string vibrates in n loops, then frequency of stationary waves will be:

blocks.final_answer: λ = 1.0 m; f₁ = 50 Hz; v = 150 m s⁻¹; 4 nodes, 3 antinodes

blocks.prompt:
13 What is an organ pipe? For an organ pipe of length l open at both ends, derive the frequencies of the fundamental mode, the second mode and the nth mode of vibration. (5 marks)
(Organ pipe kya hai? Dono siron se khuli lambai l wali organ pipe ke liye fundamental mode, doosre mode aur nth mode ki frequencies derive karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Organ pipe: hawa ka saaz jis mein khokhli lambi tube (dono sire khule ya aik band) ke hawa ke column mein stationary waves se sound banti hai. Khula sira antinode (molecules aazad); band sira node (harkat ruki).

Dono siron se khuli pipe (Fig. 7.8): dono sire antinodes. Pipe ki longitudinal waves ko transverse curves se dikhaya gaya hai jo hawa ke zarraat ka displacement aur amplitude batati hain.

(a) Fundamental mode: beech mein aik node N, dono siron par antinodes:
l = λ₁/4 + λ₁/4 = λ₁/2
λ₁ = 2l ... (7.7)
v = f₁λ₁ → f₁ = v/λ₁
f₁ = v/2l ... (7.8)
Yeh fundamental frequency ya pehla harmonic hai.

(b) Doosra mode: teen antinodes aur do nodes (Fig. 7.8 b):
l = λ₂/4 + λ₂/2 + λ₂/4 = (1 + 2 + 1)λ₂/4
λ₂ = l
f₂ = v/λ₂ = v/l = 2f₁ (kyunke v/2l = f₁)

(c) nth mode:
fₙ = n(v/2l) = nf₁
λₙ = 2l/n ... (7.9), n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, …
Yani khuli pipe poori harmonic series f₁, 2f₁, 3f₁, …, nf₁ deti hai.

book_ref.quote: As at the open end, an air molecule has complete freedom of motion so it acts as antinode

blocks.prompt:
14 An organ pipe 0.85 m long is open at both ends. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m s⁻¹, find the wavelength and frequency of the fundamental, and the frequencies of the second and third harmonics. (3 marks)
(0.85 m lambi organ pipe dono siron se khuli hai. Sound ki speed 340 m s⁻¹ le kar fundamental ki wavelength aur frequency, aur doosre aur teesre harmonic ki frequencies nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Khuli pipe mein λ₁ = 2l, f₁ = v/2l aur fₙ = nf₁, n = 1, 2, 3, …

book_ref.quote: Similarly, frequency for air column vibrating in n loops is:

blocks.final_answer: λ₁ = 1.7 m; f₁ = 200 Hz; f₂ = 400 Hz; f₃ = 600 Hz

blocks.prompt:
15 For an organ pipe of length l closed at one end, derive the frequencies of the fundamental mode, the second mode and the nth mode of vibration. Why is a pipe open at both ends richer in harmonics? (5 marks)
(Aik sire se band lambai l wali organ pipe ke liye fundamental, doosre aur nth mode ki frequencies derive karein. Dono siron se khuli pipe harmonics mein zyada amir kyun hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Aik sire se band pipe (Fig. 7.9) mein band sira node (hawa ke molecules ki harkat ruki) aur khula sira antinode hai.

(a) Fundamental mode: aik node aur aik antinode (Fig. 7.9 a):
l = λ₁/4
λ₁ = 4l ... (7.10)
v = f₁λ₁ → f₁ = v/λ₁ = v/4l
f₁ fundamental frequency hai.

(b) Doosra mode: do nodes aur do antinodes (Fig. 7.9 b):
l = λ₃/4 + λ₃/2 = (3/4)λ₃
λ₃ = 4l/3 ... (7.11)
f₃ = v/λ₃ = v/(4l/3) = 3v/4l
f₃ = 3f₁ (kyunke v/4l = f₁)
Harmonic number f/f₁ = 3 hai, is liye doosra mode teesra harmonic deta hai.

(c) nth mode:
fₙ = n(v/4l) = nf₁
λₙ = 4l/n ... (7.12), n = 1, 3, 5, …
Sirf odd harmonics hote hain.

Muqabla: khuli pipe fₙ = nf₁, n = 1, 2, 3, … (tamam harmonics) deti hai, band pipe sirf n = 1, 3, 5, … Is liye dono siron se khuli pipe harmonics mein zyada amir hai.

book_ref.quote: Then at the closed end, we get a node while at the open end, we get an antinode

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Yaad rakhein: band pipe ka 'doosra mode' teesra harmonic (3f₁) hai, doosra nahi. Harmonic number hamesha f/f₁ hota hai. Kitaab ne yahan 'second harmonic' likha hai jo ghalat hai (book correction).

blocks.prompt:
16 An organ pipe 0.17 m long is closed at one end. Taking the speed of sound as 340 m s⁻¹, find the wavelength of its fundamental mode and the frequencies of its first three modes of vibration. (3 marks)
(0.17 m lambi organ pipe aik sire se band hai. Sound ki speed 340 m s⁻¹ le kar fundamental mode ki wavelength aur pehle teen modes ki frequencies nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Band pipe mein λ₁ = 4l aur fₙ = nf₁, sirf odd n = 1, 3, 5, …

book_ref.quote: When the pipe is closed at one end then frequency for nth harmonic is:

blocks.prompt:
17 What are microwaves? Describe an experiment to demonstrate stationary waves using microwaves, and explain how the wavelength is found from it. (5 marks)
(Microwaves kya hain? Microwaves ke zariye stationary waves dikhane ka tajurba bayan karein aur batayein ke is se wavelength kaise nikalti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Microwaves: electromagnetic radiation ki aik qisam. In ki wavelengths millimetres ya centimetres ke darje ki hoti hain, radiowaves se bohat chhoti, is liye 'micro' waves.

Stationary microwaves: jab microwaves kisi cavity (wave guide, resonant chamber) mein qaid hon to aage peeche takra kar nodes aur antinodes wali standing wave banati hain. Yeh tab hota hai jab microwave frequency cavity ki resonant frequency se mile.

Tajurba (Fig. 7.10):
Saman: microwave source (transmitter), probe detector aur metal reflector (dhaat ki plate), aik line mein.
1. Source ki waves metal plate tak ja kar wapas reflect hoti hain.
2. Reflected aur incident waves mil kar stationary wave pattern banati hain.
3. Transmitter aur plate ke darmiyan probe detector ise pakarta hai; signal ki intensity detector se dekhi jaati hai.
4. Plate ya detector hila kar zyada signal (antinodes) aur kam signal (nodes) ki jagahein maloom ki jaati hain.

Wavelength: aik antinode se agle antinode ka faasla naapa jata hai. Antinodes λ/2 door hote hain (7.4), is liye λ = 2 × (antinode se antinode faasla).

book_ref.quote: The waves coming out of microwave source are moving towards the metal plate and then reflected back.

blocks.prompt:
18 In a microwave stationary wave experiment, the probe detector is moved from one antinode past four further antinodes, a total distance of 6.0 cm. Find the wavelength and frequency of the microwaves (c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹). (3 marks)
(Microwave stationary wave tajurbe mein probe detector aik antinode se aage chaar mazeed antinodes paar karta hai, kul faasla 6.0 cm. Microwaves ki wavelength aur frequency nikalein (c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹).)
blocks.explanation: Chaar mazeed antinodes paar karna yani λ/2 ke chaar faasle.

book_ref.quote: By finding the distance from one antinode to the next antinode

blocks.prompt:
19 How does the size of an opening compared with the wavelength affect the diffraction of waves? Explain with the observations in a ripple tank and give two examples of diffraction from everyday life and science. (5 marks)
(Opening ka size wavelength ke muqable mein waves ke diffraction par kya asar daalta hai? Ripple tank ke mushahidaat se wazeh karein aur rozmarra aur science se diffraction ki do misalein dein.)
blocks.explanation:
Diffraction: rukawaton ke tez kinaron ya konon ke gird waves ka murna, ya rukawat ke peeche phailna. Yeh tab hota hai jab wave wavelength ke barabar size ki rukawat ya opening (slit) se mile. Jitni lambi wavelength, utna zyada phailao. Yeh paani, sound, roshni aur doosri electromagnetic waves mein hota hai.

Ripple tank (Fig. 7.11): is mein paani, vibrator (maslan motor wali hilti sui), rukawatein (chhota rectangular block ya adh-daairi barrier) aur mukhtalif chaurai ke gaps hote hain. Vibrator daairi ya mutawazi waves banata hai; rukawat se khaas chaurai ka gap banaya jata hai aur tajurba mukhtalif gaps se dohraya jata hai.

Mushahidaat:
1. Gap wavelength se chhota: diffraction zyada; waves mur kar adh-daairi pattern banati hain.
2. Gap wavelength ke muqable mein bara: diffraction kam; waves kam mur kar guzarti hain.
Yani gap aur wavelength ka ta'alluq wave ke rawaiye ko tay karta hai.

Misalein:
(i) Konon ke peeche ya darwaze se aawaz sunayi deti hai kyunke sound waves konon ke gird murti hain.
(ii) Crystals X-rays ko diffract karte hain kyunke atoms ki qataaron ka faasla X-ray wavelength ke darje ka hai.

book_ref.quote: It occurs when a wave encounters a physical barrier or an opening (a slit)

blocks.prompt:
20 The vibrator of a ripple tank produces 360 pulses in 12 s, and the distance between successive crests is 2.0 cm. Find (i) the period (ii) the frequency (iii) the speed of the water waves. (3 marks)
(Ripple tank ka vibrator 12 s mein 360 pulses banata hai aur lagataar crests ka faasla 2.0 cm hai. Nikalein: (i) period (ii) frequency (iii) paani ki waves ki speed.)
blocks.explanation: Period fi pulse waqt; frequency us ka ulat; crests ka faasla wavelength hai, is liye v = fλ.

book_ref.quote: n = 500 pulses t = 10 s f = ?

blocks.prompt:
21 Explain, with the example of two tuning forks of 32 Hz and 28 Hz, how beats are produced and why the number of beats per second equals the frequency difference. How are beats used to find an unknown frequency or to tune an instrument? (5 marks)
(32 Hz aur 28 Hz ke do tuning forks ki misaal se wazeh karein ke beats kaise bante hain aur fi second beats frequencies ke farq ke barabar kyun hote hain. Na-maloom frequency nikalne ya saaz tune karne mein beats kaise kaam aate hain?)
blocks.explanation:
Beats: jab thori mukhtalif frequencies wali do aik simt mein chalti waves milti hain to aawaz baqaida zyada aur kam hoti hai; yeh beats hain.

Banna: tuning forks khalis note dete hain. Aik frequency (32 Hz) ke do forks A aur B aik saath bajne par aik hi note lagta hai. B par wax ya plasticene lagane se us ki frequency kam ho kar maslan 28 Hz ho jati hai. Ab aik saath bajne par baari baari tez aur dheemi hone wali aawaz (beat note) sunayi deti hai, jo dono waves ke interference se hai.

Waveforms (Fig. 7.12): (a) A ki wave, (b) B ki wave, (c) un ka resultant.
• Lamha X par dono displacements aik simt mein: bara resultant, oonchi aawaz.
• 1/8 s baad Y par displacements ulat: kam resultant, dheemi ya na hone ke barabar aawaz.
• Mazeed 1/8 s baad Z par phir aik simt mein: phir oonchi aawaz.
Yani aik oonchi aawaz se agli tak 1/4 s, yani 4 beats fi second.

Fi second beats: frequencies ka farq fA − fB = 32 − 28 = 4 Hz, beats fi second ke barabar. Is liye
fi second beats = fA − fB, aur f_beat = 1/T, jahan T = t₂ − t₁ do lagataar oonchi aawazon ka waqfa hai.
Farq 10 Hz se zyada ho to beats pehchanna mushkil hai.

Istemal:
(i) Na-maloom frequency: na-maloom fork ko maloom fork ke saath bajayein; f₂ = f₁ ± (fi second beats). Aik fork par wax se us ki frequency ghatti hai; beats ke barhne ya ghatne se sahi qeemat ka pata chalta hai.
(ii) Tuning: piano ya violin ki string maloom note ke saath bajayi jaati hai aur kasi ya dheeli ki jaati hai jab tak beats band na hon.

book_ref.quote: This note is called beat note or a beat which is due to interference between the sound waves

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Kitaab ne X se Y tak 1/4 s likha hai; asal mein 4 beats fi second mein aik oonchi se agli oonchi aawaz tak 1/4 s hai, is liye oonchi se dheemi tak sirf 1/8 s (book correction).

blocks.prompt:

(384 Hz ka tuning fork A doosre fork B ke saath 5 beats fi second deta hai. B par thori wax lagane se beats 3 fi second ho jaate hain. Nikalein: (i) loading se pehle B ki frequency (ii) loading se pehle do lagataar oonchi aawazon ka waqfa.)
blocks.explanation: B ki do mumkin qeematein fA ± 5; wax B ko ghatati hai, to woh qeemat lein jis mein B ghat kar 384 Hz ke qareeb aaye.

book_ref.quote: When first fork is loaded with wax, the frequency of first fork must fall below 256 Hz

steps: Wax fB ko ghatati hai. 379 Hz hota to 384 se door ho kar beats 5 se barh jaate.
389 Hz ho to 384 ke qareeb aa kar beats ghat kar 3 hote hain, jaisa dekha gaya; is liye fB = 389 Hz

blocks.prompt:
23 Define intensity of a wave and state its unit. Show that I = P/A, and explain why the intensity of a mechanical wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude. What is a progressive wave? (5 marks)
(Wave ki intensity ki definition aur unit likhein. Sabit karein ke I = P/A, aur wazeh karein ke mechanical wave ki intensity amplitude ke square ke mutanasib kyun hai. Progressive wave kya hai?)
blocks.explanation:
Progressive wave: woh wave jo medium mein aik simt mein chalti aur energy aik jagah se doosri jagah le jaati hai, stationary wave ke baraks. Misalein: paani, sound, light waves.

Intensity: progressive wave ke phailne ki simt mein fi unit area fi unit time muntaqil hone wali energy. Yeh wave ki power ka paimana hai, I se zahir aur W m⁻² mein naapi jaati hai.

Expression: definition se
I = E/(A × t)
I = (E/t)/A
I = P/A (kyunke E/t = P)
jahan E = energy (J), t = waqt (s), P = power (W), A = area (m²). Agar waves source se har taraf yaksaan phailein to A kurre (sphere) ka sathi area 4πr² hai, is liye I = P/(4πr²).

Intensity aur amplitude: mechanical waves mein energy medium ke zarraat ki kinetic aur potential energy ki shakal mein jama hoti hai, aur us ki miqdaar zarraat ke displacement (amplitude) par munhasir hai. Is liye
I ∝ A²
I = kA² ... (7.13)
jahan k constant hai jo wave aur medium ki khususiyaat par munhasir hai.

Note: chalti wave ki frequency aur amplitude aazad hain, is liye aawaz (amplitude) barh sakti hai aur pitch (frequency) wahi rehti hai.

book_ref.quote: Intensity is defined as the amount of energy transmitted per unit area per unit time

blocks.prompt:
24 A small source emits 80 W of sound evenly in all directions. Find (i) the area of the sphere at 4.0 m (ii) the intensity at 4.0 m (iii) the intensity at that point if the amplitude of the waves there were doubled. (3 marks)
(Aik chhota source 80 W sound har taraf yaksaan deta hai. Nikalein: (i) 4.0 m par kurre ka area (ii) 4.0 m par intensity (iii) agar wahan waves ka amplitude dugna ho jaye to intensity.)
blocks.explanation: Power ko 4πr² par phailayein, phir amplitude ki tabdeeli ke liye I ∝ A².
steps: I = kA²: amplitude dugna to I chaar guna: I′ = 4 × 0.398 = 1.6 W m⁻²

blocks.prompt:
25 What is the Doppler effect? Derive an expression for the apparent frequency heard by a stationary observer when a source of sound moves towards the observer, and show that the pitch rises. (5 marks)
(Doppler effect kya hai? Jab sound ka source thehre observer ki taraf aaye to observer ko sunayi dene wali zahiri frequency ka formula derive karein aur dikhayein ke pitch barhti hai.)
blocks.explanation:
Doppler effect: source aur observer (sunne wale) ki nisbati harkat se waves ki frequency (pitch) mein zahiri tabdeeli. Misaal: platform ki taraf aate engine ki seeti oonchi aur door jaate ki neechi.

Saakin source: saakin source S λ wavelength ki waves v speed se deta hai. Thehra observer fi second
f = v/λ
waves leta hai.

Source uₛ velocity se thehre observer C ki taraf (Fig. 7.12): waves dab jaati hain kyunke utni hi waves kam jagah mein aa jaati hain. Fi second wavelength mein kami (Doppler shift):
Δλ = uₛ/f
C ko milne wali wavelength:
λ_C = λ − Δλ
λ_C = v/f − uₛ/f
λ_C = (v − uₛ)/f
Zahiri frequency (C ko fi second milne wali waves):
f_C = v/λ_C
f_C = v/[(v − uₛ)/f]
f_C = [v/(v − uₛ)] f

Chunke v/(v − uₛ) > 1, is liye f_C > f. Zahiri frequency barhti hai, yani aawaz ki pitch oonchi ho jati hai.

book_ref.quote: The compression of the waves is due to the fact that same number of waves are contained in a shorter space

blocks.prompt:
26 A motorcycle horn of frequency 620 Hz approaches a stationary listener at 30 m s⁻¹ (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹). Find (i) the Doppler shift Δλ (ii) the wavelength reaching the listener (iii) the frequency heard. (3 marks)

blocks.explanation: Δλ = uₛ/f, phir λ_C = (v − uₛ)/f aur f_C = v/λ_C.

blocks.prompt:
27 Derive an expression for the apparent frequency heard by a stationary observer when a source of sound moves away from the observer, and show that the pitch falls. Compare the result with the case of an approaching source. (5 marks)
(Jab sound ka source thehre observer se door jaye to sunayi dene wali zahiri frequency ka formula derive karein aur dikhayein ke pitch ghatti hai. Natije ka qareeb aate source se muqabla karein.)
blocks.explanation:
Source f frequency aur λ = v/f wavelength ki waves deta hai, v sound ki speed hai.

Source uₛ velocity se thehre observer D se door (Fig. 7.12): waves phail jaati hain kyunke utni hi waves ab zyada faasle mein hoti hain. Fi second wavelength mein izafa (Doppler shift):
Δλ = uₛ/f
D ko milne wali wavelength:
λ_D = λ + Δλ
λ_D = v/f + uₛ/f = (v + uₛ)/f
Zahiri frequency:
f_D = v/λ_D
f_D = v/[(v + uₛ)/f]
f_D = [v/(v + uₛ)] f

Chunke v/(v + uₛ) < 1, is liye f_D < f. Zahiri frequency ghatti hai, yani pitch neechi.

Muqabla: qareeb aata source: λ_C = (v − uₛ)/f, f_C = [v/(v − uₛ)] f > f (pitch oonchi); door jata source: λ_D = (v + uₛ)/f, f_D = [v/(v + uₛ)] f < f (pitch neechi).

book_ref.quote: where Δλ is the increase in wavelength in one second and is called Doppler shift.

blocks.title: Wazahat
blocks.text: Kitaab mein Case 2 par λ_D = uₛ/f chhapa hai; yeh ghalat hai. uₛ/f sirf Doppler shift Δλ hai, aur D ko milne wali wavelength λ_D = λ + Δλ = (v + uₛ)/f hai (book correction).

blocks.prompt:
28 A bus sounds its horn (900 Hz) at a stop and then moves off with uniform acceleration. 40 s later the horn is sounded again and a passenger waiting at the stop hears 850 Hz. Find the bus's speed at that moment and its distance from the stop (speed of sound 340 m s⁻¹). (3 marks)
(Aik bus stop par horn (900 Hz) bajati hai phir yaksaan acceleration se chal parti hai. 40 s baad horn phir bajta hai aur stop par khare musafir ko 850 Hz sunayi deta hai. Us waqt bus ki speed aur stop se faasla nikalein (sound ki speed 340 m s⁻¹).)
blocks.explanation: Bus door ja rahi hai, is liye speed ke liye f′ = [v/(v + uₛ)] f; aaram se yaksaan acceleration mein S = average velocity × waqt.

blocks.prompt:
29 Describe the applications of the Doppler effect in (i) RADAR (ii) SONAR (iii) astronomy (red shift and blue shift) (iv) the radar speed trap. (5 marks)
(Doppler effect ke istemal bayan karein: (i) RADAR (ii) SONAR (iii) falkiyat (red shift aur blue shift) (iv) radar speed trap.)
blocks.explanation:
Doppler effect sound ke ilawa electromagnetic waves par bhi laagu hai.

(i) RADAR (RAdio Detection And Ranging): radio waves bhejne aur lene wala aala jo hawai jahaz ki oonchai aur speed batata hai. Jahaz qareeb aaye to reflected wavelength chhoti, door jaye to lambi (Fig. 7.13). Satellites ki speed bhi isi usool se.

(ii) SONAR (Sound Navigation And Ranging): paani ke andar sonic ya ultrasonic echo-ranging; sound ki goonj se cheezon ka pata. Doppler detection target aur detector ki nisbati speed se target ki speed batati hai. Fauji istemal: submarines ka pata aur maqam, antisubmarine hathiyaron ka control, mine hunting; samandar ki gehraai bhi.

(iii) Falkiyat: sitare ke line spectrum ka lab source se muqabla kar ke Doppler shift aur us se speed nikalti hai.
• Door jaate sitare red shift: lambi wavelength, spectrum laal sire ki taraf. Tamam door ki galaxies red shift dikhati hain, yani hum se door ja rahi hain.
• Qareeb aate sitare blue shift: chhoti wavelength, spectrum neele sire ki taraf (Fig. 7.14).

(iv) Radar speed trap: microwaves chhote bursts mein bhej kar raaste ki gaari se reflect hoti hain. Chalti gaari se reflection Doppler shift hota hai; shift naap kar computer gaari ki speed nikalta hai.

Doosre istemal: satellite navigation aur communication, hawa aur barish ke liye Doppler radar, khoon ke bahao ke liye Doppler ultrasound aur echocardiography.

book_ref.quote: Doppler effect is also applicable to electromagnetic waves.

blocks.prompt:
30 A spectral line measured as 400 nm in the laboratory is observed at 440 nm in the light of a distant galaxy. (i) Is the galaxy approaching or receding? (ii) Using f′ = [c/(c + uₛ)] f with c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, find its speed. (3 marks)
(Lab mein 400 nm wali spectral line aik door ki galaxy ki roshni mein 440 nm par milti hai. (i) Galaxy qareeb aa rahi hai ya door ja rahi hai? (ii) f′ = [c/(c + uₛ)] f aur c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ se us ki speed nikalein.)
blocks.explanation: Dono wavelengths ko f = c/λ se frequency mein badlein; λ′ > λ yani red shift; phir Doppler formula se uₛ.

book_ref.quote: (b) Compute the speed of the galaxy relative to the Earth.

steps: λ′ > λ (f′ < f): red shift, galaxy Zameen se door ja rahi hai
c + uₛ = c f/f′ = 3.3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹
blocks.final_answer: Door ja rahi hai (red shift); uₛ = 3.0 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹
